rationale: Migration 552 alone, split out of round-1 correlation f5550f04 because bundling it with A1's nine files forced the compression that drew that round's gating objections (and the guardian's edit-8 medium named the bundling itself). One edit: a second UPDATE trigger on migration 357's existing archive function, firing exactly when 357's cannot — content_data changed, rendered_html did not — so the one change the content-loss class is about stops being the one change the archive cannot see. The ROLLBACK sidecar exists (552_..._ROLLBACK.sql, drops the trigger only, archived rows KEPT per the 344/357 precedent) and is not an edit entry because it is not the change (COUNCIL_SCOPE_NOT_THE_CHANGE_RE). Answers to the round-1 objections that touched this half. GUARDIAN medium (fail-closed on a table every pipeline writes; a hidden content-only writer would hard-block; blast radius unverifiable from the guardian's seat): the exposure is NOT new — 357 already fail-closes every rendered_html-changing UPDATE and every DELETE on this table, so a broken history table ALREADY halts every pipeline's page writes; 552 adds a new FIRING CONDITION to an existing posture, not a new failure mode, and the posture is 357's own reviewed choice (RFC_017: halt loudly rather than silently recreate the loss class). Measured blast radius of the new arm, restated with its query so the seat need not trust the assertion: writers were censused by grep at HEAD (every Go in-place writer sets rendered_html in the same UPDATE; only the admin handler's dynamic SET list can produce a content-only UPDATE), and the entire in-place overwrite volume is 316 archive rows in 14 days fleet-wide (~23/day) — the content-only arm's volume is a subset of admin edits, i.e. single digits daily at most. A hidden content-only writer, should one exist, is precisely the writer the content-loss detector exists to expose, and its writes would hard-block only if the history table itself were broken — the state in which 357 has already halted everything else. REUSE_AGENT low (prior council precedent on 357 not checked before an adjacent change): checked this round and cited — 357 shipped under bugs_open/229's owner ruling (candidate 1, 'extend the 344 shape'); its own header records the RFC_017 fail-closed precedent and the first-apply probe failure on same-xact created_at ordering, which this migration's probe inherits the fix for (rows selected BY BYTES). DEBUG_HISTORIAN low (no stated pg_proc/pg_trigger existence check): the shipped file HAS the full pre-flight — a DO block that RAISEs unless page_component_artefact_archive() exists, unless 357's UPDATE trigger exists (the mutual-exclusion argument depends on it), and IF the 552 trigger already exists (idempotence); round 1's sketch elided it and this round's sketch carries it. Deliberate redundancy stated rather than discovered: the content-only arm archives the unchanged rendered_html bytes beside the pre-image content, chosen over a parameterised second code path through a fail-closed function; volume is watched daily by the content-loss-check heartbeat's pair counts. Committed e7567d1fc, NOT applied; apply follows this verdict.

plan.risks: Fail-closed: a broken page_component_history halts content-only page writes loudly — the same state in which 357's arms have already halted every rendered_html write and every delete, so no pipeline acquires a failure mode it did not already have; what it acquires is a new firing condition whose live producer is admin edits (single digits daily). The content-only arm stores the unchanged rendered_html bytes beside the pre-image content — deliberate redundancy over a second code path through a fail-closed function; growth is reported daily by the content-loss-check heartbeat's pair counts. The probe runs inside the migration transaction against a throwaway row on the oldest page and self-cleans; it inherits 357's by-bytes selection precisely because ordering by created_at failed 357's own first apply.
